questions.context: In a class in Medellín, children talk about soccer, basketball and swimming after school.

options.feedback: Pizza, rice and juice are foods and drinks, not sports.
Soccer, basketball and swimming are all sports.
Guitar, drums and piano are musical instruments, not sports.
Dog, cat and bird are animals, not sports.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta repasa vocabulario básico de deportes en inglés. También ayuda a clasificar palabras de deportes, comidas y música sin confusión.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Bogotá, Sara says: "I love dancing vallenato at family parties."

options.feedback: "Hates" means she dislikes it strongly, the opposite of love.
"Never dances" contradicts her happy statement about parties.
"Love" means a very strong like for an activity.
She mentions vallenato at parties, so she knows this music.

questions.explanation: El verbo love expresa un gusto muy fuerte por una actividad. También se diferencia de like y hate en opiniones personales en inglés.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence.
questions.context: In Cali, Diego talks about his free time: "I like _____ soccer with my friends."

options.feedback: After "like" we need the -ing form, not the base form alone.
"Like" is followed by verb plus -ing, so "playing" is correct.
"Played" is past tense and is not used after "like" here.
"Plays" is third person present and is not correct after "like".

questions.explanation: Los verbos like, love y hate se combinan con la forma -ing del verbo. También se practica esta regla con actividades deportivas cotidianas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does Luisa like and dislike?
questions.context: In Cartagena, students read: "Luisa loves reading comics. She hates running in the morning."

options.text: She loves running and hates reading.
options.feedback: The text says the opposite about reading and running.

options.text: She loves comics and loves running.
options.feedback: She hates running, so she does not love both activities.

options.text: She loves reading comics and hates running.
options.feedback: "Loves" shows her like and "hates" shows her strong dislike.

options.text: She hates comics and hates reading.
options.feedback: She loves reading comics, so this option is incorrect.

questions.explanation: La lectura exige identificar gustos con love y disgustos con hate. También se trabaja la comprensión literal de frases cortas sobre pasatiempos.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the correct short answer if his friend loves bandeja paisa?
questions.context: At recess in Bucaramanga, a boy asks his friend about favorite food: "Do you like bandeja paisa?"

options.feedback: "No, I do" is contradictory and not a correct short answer.
"Hates" is negative and the grammar "I hates" is wrong.

options.text: Yes, I do. I love it.
options.feedback: "Yes, I do" answers the question and "I love it" gives the opinion.
"Love it not" has incorrect word order in English.

questions.explanation: Las respuestas cortas con Yes I do y No I do not son esenciales. También se añade una opinión con love para expresar gustos por comidas colombianas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which rule is correct about these sentences?
questions.context: In Pereira, a teacher writes: "I like listening to salsa. I hate watching boring shows."

options.text: Like and hate use the base verb without -ing.
options.feedback: Both sentences use listening and watching with -ing.

options.text: Like and hate use verb plus -ing for activities.
options.feedback: "Listening" and "watching" follow like and hate correctly.

options.text: Like uses -ing but hate uses past tense.
options.feedback: Hate also uses -ing here, not past tense.

options.text: Like and hate never use verbs after them.
options.feedback: Both sentences have verbs after like and hate.

questions.explanation: El análisis confirma que like y hate piden verbo con ing. También se observan ejemplos con música y televisión para fijar la estructura.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Who has a different opinion about spicy ají if two friends love it?
questions.context: In Santa Marta, three friends talk: "I love surfing. I like playing guitar. I hate eating spicy ají."

options.text: The friend who hates eating spicy ají.
options.feedback: "Hates" is the opposite opinion to "love" about ají.
Surfing is a sport and does not show an opinion about ají.

options.text: The friend who likes playing guitar.
options.feedback: Playing guitar is music and does not talk about ají.

options.text: All friends have the same opinion.
options.feedback: Hate and love are opposite, so opinions are different.

questions.explanation: Comparar opiniones exige distinguir like, love y hate en contexto. También se analizan gustos sobre deportes, música y comida colombiana.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question best asks for an opinion?
questions.context: In Manizales, a student wants to ask for opinions politely: "What do you think about cumbia music?"

options.feedback: This is an order, not a question about opinions.

options.text: You like cumbia or not, answer.
options.feedback: This question is rude and the grammar is not polite.

options.text: What is your favorite music? Do you like cumbia?
options.feedback: These questions are polite and clearly ask for an opinion.
This sentence pushes a negative opinion instead of asking openly.

questions.explanation: Pedir opiniones requiere preguntas abiertas y un tono cortés. También se valora proponer opciones sin imponer el propio gusto musical.
questions.subject: ingles
